case_name: Ramesh Yadav v District Magistrate, Etah and Others
facts: This application under Art. 32 of the Constitution is directed against the order of detention of the petitioner under S. 3(2) of the National Security Act, and was made at a time when the petitioner had already been in Mainpuri Jail as an under trial prisoner in connection with certain pending criminal cases.
A return has been made to the rule nisi and the detaining authority has justified his order.
Five grounds were advanced in support of the order of detention. They are:
The detenu is an active member of the inter-District gang enlisted as No. I.D. 64;
On January 8, 1983, information was received by the police that a gang of dacoits were present in Village Kapreta.

In the grounds of detention, apart from specifying the above five grounds, reference was made to the fact that the detenu creates public terror on account of his criminal activities which are absolutely prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
Five grounds were indicated of which four are referable to specific incidents. Of these four, three are of 1980, prior to the making of the previous order of detention.

On a reading of the grounds, particularly the paragraph which we have extracted above, it is clear that the order of detention was passed as the detaining authority was apprehensive that in case the detenu was released on bail he would again carry on his criminal activities in the area.
petitioner_arguments: The impugned order, therefore, has to be quashed.
We allow the writ petition and direct that the petitioner be set at liberty forthwith unless he is in lawful detention otherwise.
Merely on the ground that an accused in detention as an undertrial prisoner was likely to get bail an order of detention under the National Security Act should not ordinarily be passed.
respondent_arguments: The detaining authority has justified his order.
Thereupon the writ petition has been filed.
A return has been made to the rule nisi and the detaining authority has justified his order.
court_reasoning: We the petitioner that the order of detention in the circumstances is not sustainable and is contrary to the well settled principles indicated by this Court in series of cases relating to preventive detention.
If the apprehension of the detaining authority was true, the bail application had to be opposed and in case bail was granted, challenge against that order in the higher forum had to be raised.
holding: The impugned order has to be quashed.
The petitioner be set at liberty forthwith unless he is in lawful detention otherwise.
